blockers: Pricing, Docs, and Sign in links expose no functional signup, dashboard, subscription, or checkout flow; likely route names return 404.
The OpenAPI specification contains generation and catalog endpoints only—no account, provisioning, checkout, payment, or x402 endpoint.
Documentation says human developers must create an account and pay monthly by card, but the absent onboarding flow prevents verifying CAPTCHA, email confirmation, KYC, or other gates.
Numeric overage rates and enterprise pricing are not disclosed.
trust_events: Would warn before supplying payment details: drift-flight.org was registered on 2026-07-20, less than three weeks before this review, and has no meaningful independent web footprint.

Would require merchant verification: the claimed operator, Driftflight Studio, Inc., has no disclosed address, incorporation jurisdiction, registration number, or independently verifiable company record.
The advertised customer companies and testimonials could not be independently verified.
The domain publishes no MX record despite listing legal@drift-flight.org and privacy@drift-flight.org as its only contacts.
Licensing language conflicts: marketing says every paid render has a commercial licence, while pricing and terms restrict Hobby output to personal, non-commercial use.
notes: Primary service: a text-to-image API with shared/private style presets and hosted image URLs. Read-only API GETs for models and presets worked. Listed plans are Hobby at $5/month for 100 generations, Studio at $29/month for 750, and Agency at $119/month for 3,000; billing is monthly in advance and annual billing purportedly saves 20%. The site does not explicitly identify the dollar currency. No actionable purchase or programmatic payment/provisioning path exists, so the directive cannot be completed end-to-end as an agent.
